To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the effect of repeated seizures in the kindling preparation on drug response is variable and depends on the seizure type, the stimulation parameters, and the drug tested; and (ii) drug response is not necessarily decreased following repeated seizures, and in fact may be enhanced.
the effect of repeated seizures (pretreatment) on drug response (ED50): (1) is drug-specific, (2) is seizure-type-specific, and (3) depends upon the number of pretreatment stimulations.
(1) repeated focal seizures do not lead to an increase in anticonvulsive dose (ED50); and (2) repeated focal seizures may actually lead to a decrease or an increase in antiepileptic dose (ED50).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of antiepileptic drugs in the kindling preparation.
the study of the mechanisms of action of anticonvulsive drugs.
the effects of repeated seizures on subsequent drug response, and the implications of these effects for the treatment of epilepsy.

, in the kindling preparation, drug response is enhanced after repeated focal seizures, and not decreased.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kindling model is a good model to study drug effects, but that it is not a good model to predict the outcome of drug treatment.
the kindling model is a good model for the study of the effects of repeated seizures on the anticonvulsants.

the kindling paradigm is a useful tool in the study of the anticonvulsants.
